changes.before: Implement sessionActive(session,now). Match the worked contract and the changed-input checks without modifying the supplied input values.
changes.after: Treat a session as expired at its exact expiry time.

before: An expiry time defines when a session stops being valid. This contract treats the exact expiry instant as expired.
This exercise is a small pure JavaScript model. Its inputs are supplied directly; it does not receive live HTTP requests, operate a database, or deploy a service.

now and expiresAt use the same supplied time unit. The strict less-than comparison excludes equality. A real service needs a trusted clock and validated session data; browser-provided time is not an authority.

Read the function call sessionActive({"expiresAt":100}, 99) from the inside out: the arguments supply the inputs, sessionActive runs the body once, and return sends its result back to the caller. console.log displays that result; it does not change it.
now equals expiresAt. Is the session active? The accepted interval ends before expiresAt. Equality is outside it.
after: An expiry time marks when a session stops being valid. This rule accepts it only before that moment. At the expiry time itself, the session is already expired.
now and expiresAt must use the same time unit. A real server uses its trusted time and verified session data. The caller's browser must not choose the time used for this security check.
The < comparison means strictly before. When now equals expiresAt, it returns false. A later time also returns false.
session && ... prevents reading expiresAt when the session is missing. Boolean turns the whole result into true or false, including false for a missing session.
Complete sessionActive(session, now). Require a session and a current time strictly before expiresAt. Test before, at, and after the limit without changing the inputs.
